results.1: exit 0; becomes `coder: retired`. `# main model` and the interior temperature comment are gone; `# trailing comment after coder` stays, still indented under it
results.2: all five arms: same as route 1

examples.before:
tools:
  - lint
  # between lint and test
  - test
  - deploy
  # after tools

results.1: exit 0; `- test` and `- deploy` removed; `# between lint and test` and `# after tools` both kept
results.2: three arms: same as route 1; two arms: also delete `# between lint and test`, leaving only `- lint` and `# after tools`
all five arms: same as route 1

results.1: exit 0 (not refused with exit 3); becomes `x: 7,` and `# comment on y` is silently deleted
results.2: all five arms: same as route 1

results.1: exit 0; logs the `set agents.coder` entry, then removals of `agents.coder.model` and `agents.coder.temperature` with their old values
results.2: four arms: same order as route 1; one arm: logs the two removals before the set

context.in_practice: On this run, route 1 did not do what it says. Its description promises exit 3 when a deletion inside `{...}` text spans several lines. Instead it made the `multi.x` change, exited 0, and dropped the comment, exactly as every route-2 arm did. The only file difference between the routes is the comment between list items. Route 1 and three route-2 arms keep it; two route-2 arms delete it.
context.stakes: Replacing a section with a single value deletes its old entries. The question is which nearby comments disappear along with them, and whether a change inside multi-line `{...}` text is refused or done anyway, silently dropping a comment.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 keeps comments between list items but did not refuse the multi-line `{...}` edit it says it refuses. Route 2 is inconsistent across arms: two of five also delete comments between list items.

plan_why: Replaces collections with smaller values to show which lines a deletion removes. A block mapping shows whether the interior comment goes and the trailing comment stays. A block list shows the same for list items. A one-line flow map shows a flow deletion on one line, and a flow map spread over several lines shows whether the program refuses with exit 3 or rewrites it (possibly losing its comment).
routes: Whole block lines (interior comments go, trailing ones stay); a flow deletion only on one line, otherwise exit 3
